diagnostic_tracker.title: Pattern Parade — Day 1 Diagnostic Checklist
diagnostic_tracker.when_used: During Lesson 1, while children are in the partner-build phase of the Action segment.
diagnostic_tracker.usage_notes: Walk between pairs during the partner-build activity. For each child, tick the columns where you see clear evidence; leave blank if not yet observed (rather than marking 'no'). The 'Creates pattern (independent)' column is the key signal for which children are already operating above grade — these can be challenged during Lessons 2–5. Children with blanks across the first three columns may need a small-group re-loop on Lesson 1 before continuing.
diagnostic_tracker.layout_description: One letter page, portrait orientation. Title at the top, expectation focus (A7.1) in a small box below. A date field and class label in the header row. The body is a table with one column for student names (left, ~1.5in wide), four narrow tick columns (~0.9in each) labelled with the column names, and a Notes column on the right (~2in wide). Approximately 24 blank student rows so the page accommodates a typical Ontario K class.

formative_trackers.title: Pattern Parade — Lesson 2 Formative Tracker (Finding the Core)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 2, while children are in the partner phase of Lasso the Core.
columns: Explains why it is the core
formative_trackers.usage_notes: Stop at each pair. Ask 'Where is the core?' and 'How do you know?' to elicit the third column. Tick when you see clear evidence; leave blank if not observed. Children who can identify and loop but cannot explain are often almost-there — give them one more opportunity to articulate before moving on. The non-pattern recognition column is the deepest signal — children who recognize a non-pattern have internalized that the core requires repetition.
formative_trackers.layout_description: Identical layout to the diagnostic tracker but with the Lesson 2 column names. Title and expectation box updated to reflect A7.2 focus.

formative_trackers.title: Pattern Parade — Lesson 3 Formative Tracker (Same Core, Different Ways)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 3, while pairs are translating their core into sound and body versions in the Action phase.
formative_trackers.usage_notes: Translation columns should reflect whether the structural core is preserved, not whether the surface elements look polished. A child who claps clap-stomp-clap-stomp matching their AB animal pattern has succeeded — even if the claps are loud or quiet. The 'Names what stayed the same / changed' columns capture metacognition: if a child can articulate it (in any words), they have crossed the abstraction line.
formative_trackers.layout_description: Identical layout to the diagnostic tracker but with the Lesson 3 column names. Title and expectation box updated to reflect A7.3 focus.

Expectation box reads 'Expectation: A7.3 — show that patterns can be represented in different ways because the core remains the same'. 24 blank student rows. B&W line art, full page.

formative_trackers.title: Pattern Parade — Lesson 4 Formative Tracker (Fix and Extend)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 4, while pairs are working through the Fix-It and Stretch-It phases.
formative_trackers.usage_notes: The columns are deliberately separated by gap position because difficulty differs: middle and end are easier than start; forward is easier than backward. A child solid on middle/end and forward but blank on start/backward is on track for the typical K trajectory — these skills sometimes don't fully consolidate until Grade 1. Use this tracker to identify children who already extend backward independently (ready for the summative on confidence) versus children who will need conferences in Lesson 5.
formative_trackers.layout_description: Identical layout to the diagnostic tracker but with the Lesson 4 column names (one extra column compared to L2/L3 because Fix and Extend each have multiple sub-skills). Title and expectation box updated to reflect A7.4 focus.

Expectation box reads 'Expectation: A7.4 — extend patterns in both directions and identify any missing elements'. 24 blank student rows. B&W line art, full page.

summative_rubric.title: Pattern Parade — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: Used during and after Lesson 5 (Lead Your Own Parade) to score each child against all four expectations on a 4-level scale. Aligned with Ontario Kindergarten Communication of Learning conventions: descriptive, observational, growth-oriented.

levels.descriptor: With significant adult prompting, names what comes next in a 2-element repeating pattern only some of the time. Does not yet create patterns independently.
Predicts what comes next in a 2-element pattern most of the time. Creates an AB pattern with teacher prompts and a partner.
Confidently predicts and describes a repeating pattern. Independently creates an AB pattern using two animals and explains the order.
Spontaneously creates patterns with 3-element cores or longer and applies them in play. Notices patterns in the classroom environment without being asked.

rows.expectation_text: identify the core of a repeating pattern and describe why it is important

levels.descriptor: Cannot consistently isolate the core. May circle the entire strip or just one cell when asked to find the core.
Identifies the core in simple AB patterns with adult support. Struggles with ABB or ABC cores.
Independently identifies the core in AB, ABB, and ABC patterns. Explains that the core is 'the part that repeats.'
Articulates why the core matters (e.g. 'once you know the core, you can keep the parade going forever') and uses the core to predict beyond what is shown.

rows.expectation_text: show that patterns can be represented in different ways because the core remains the same

levels.descriptor: Treats different representations of the same core as different patterns. Surface-feature thinking dominates ('they are not the same because one has bears').
With teacher modelling, can produce a second version of a given core, but the structure often drifts (e.g., AB animal turns into ABB sound).
Independently translates one core into 2 different representations (animal / sound / body) while preserving the core.
Translates one core into 3 or more representations and articulates that the structure (the core) is what makes them the same — not the surface elements.

rows.expectation_text: extend patterns in both directions and identify any missing elements

levels.descriptor: Cannot fill missing elements. May put random animals in gaps. Does not yet extend patterns.
Fills missing elements at the end of a pattern (predicting next) but struggles with middle and start positions. Forward extension only.
Fills missing elements anywhere in a pattern. Extends a pattern forward correctly. May still need prompts for backward extension.
Independently extends patterns in both directions, including reasoning backward, and explains how the core determines what came before the start.

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Score during the Lesson 5 Plan-Build-Translate phases (mostly visible from the worksheet) and confirm during the Lead phase (partner observation). Level 3 is the grade-level expectation; aim for most children to land at L2 or L3 by end-of-unit. L1 is a signal for additional support; L4 is a signal for enrichment in Grade 1. Communicate scores to families using the Communication of Learning narrative format ('demonstrates a developing understanding of...') rather than letter grades.
summative_rubric.layout_description: One letter page, landscape orientation, with a 4×4 grid table (4 expectation rows × 4 level columns) plus a left-most column for the expectation code and text. Each cell contains the level descriptor in K-readable type. Title at the top of the page; usage notes printed below the table. Total table approximately 10in wide × 6in tall.

summative_task_script.title: Lead Your Own Parade — Summative Administration Guide
summative_task_script.purpose: Ties the Lesson 5 worksheet, the lesson plan's four phases (Plan-Build-Translate-Lead), and the rubric together. Tells the teacher exactly what evidence to look for during each phase and which expectation each phase's evidence maps to.
administration_steps: Before the lesson: photocopy one summative worksheet ('Lead Your Own Parade') per child. Print one rubric per child or maintain a single class rubric on a clipboard with student-name rows pre-filled. Have the Junior Pattern Conductor certificates printed and ready for the closing ceremony (do not show them to children before they have earned them).

Phase 1 (Plan, 5 min): Children draw their core in the My Core box and loop it. This produces visible evidence for A7.2. Walk the room and check that each child has identified a core; nudge children who have drawn random animals.

Phase 2 (Build, 10 min): Children fill the 8-cell parade strip extending their core forward and backward. This produces visible evidence for A7.1 (creates a pattern) and A7.4 (extends in both directions). Begin one-on-one rubric conferences during this phase — ask each child to read their parade aloud and answer 'what comes after the last animal? what came before the first animal?'.

Phase 3 (Translate, 5 min): Children translate the same core into a sound or body version on the second strip. This produces visible evidence for A7.3. Continue rubric conferences. By the end of Phase 3, you should have scored most children on at least 3 of 4 expectations.

Phase 4 (Lead, 5 min): Children pair up on the carpet and lead each other through their parade. Listen for partners articulating the core, predicting next, and predicting before. Use this phase to confirm scores you were uncertain about and to upgrade scores where a child demonstrates Level 4 thinking aloud.

After the lesson: review the rubric with the worksheet artifact in front of you. For any child below Level 3 on any expectation, note what evidence (or absence) drove that decision. Use this for the Communication of Learning narrative.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Use the worksheet as primary evidence and the partner-lead conversation as confirming evidence. For each expectation, ask: 'What level of independence and confidence did this child show?' Level 3 is the grade-level goal — aim for most children to land at L2 or L3. Children who are L4 on every expectation are ready for Grade 1 pattern work; document this for the receiving teacher. Children who are L1 on multiple expectations need targeted small-group work in the next math block — do not retain them in K patterns; instead build the bridge in concrete play and revisit.

evidence_per_expectation.A7.1: Look at Part 2 of the worksheet (Build the parade). Did the child create a valid repeating pattern across the 8 cells? Combined with Part 1 (the core they invented). A child who fills Part 2 with a coherent repetition of their Part 1 core is at Level 3 on A7.1.
evidence_per_expectation.A7.2: Look at Part 1 (My Core box). Did the child identify a core, and is it correctly looped? Then check Part 2 — does the parade actually use that core consistently? Children who looped 1 cell or the entire strip are at L1; children who looped a valid 2-3 cell core are at L3 minimum.
evidence_per_expectation.A7.3: Look at Part 3 (Show it another way). Does the second representation use the SAME structural core as Part 2? A child who fills Part 3 with sounds or bodies that follow the same AB / ABB / ABC structure is at Level 3. A child who drifts in structure (AB → ABB) is at Level 2.
evidence_per_expectation.A7.4: Look at Part 2 cells 1–2 (backward extension) and 7–8 (forward extension). Combined with the partner-lead conversation in Phase 4 ('what came before? what comes after?'). A child who fills all 8 cells correctly AND can articulate what came before the first animal is at Level 3 or 4.

certificate.title: Junior Pattern Conductor Certificate
certificate.recipient_field_label: This certificate is proudly presented to:
certificate.achievement_text: For successfully completing the 5-Day Pattern Parade unit and demonstrating the skills of a Pattern Conductor. A pattern parade certificate. Coco the Conductor congratulates the student.
skills_demonstrated: Finding the core — the part of the pattern that repeats
Showing one core in many different ways (animals, sounds, and bodies)
Fixing missing animals and extending parades in both directions
certificate.layout_description: One letter page, portrait orientation. Decorative ornamental border around the entire page (~0.5in margin). Title 'Junior Pattern Conductor Certificate' at the top in large ornate font (~1in tall). Below: the recipient label and a wide blank line for the child's name. Below: 'For successfully completing the 5-Day Pattern Parade unit and demonstrating the skills of a Pattern Conductor.' Below: a bullet list of the four skills demonstrated. Toward the bottom: two side-by-side signature lines labelled 'Teacher Signature' and 'Date'. At the bottom-centre, a small Coco the Conductor illustration holding his baton. Designed to feel celebratory and ceremonial — not utilitarian.

image_placeholders.description: A decorative ornamental border framing the certificate page, approximately 0.5in inset from each edge. Suitable for a Kindergarten celebration without feeling baby-ish.
